audit.whatIsWrong: Mega Adhesive is described as a move-speed ability in seven strings — "his move-speed W", "his W move speed plus poison sustain", "Mega Adhesive plus permanent W move speed", "blink-suppress him through his W move speed", "a champion whose entire identity is W move speed", and twice more in whys[1] and whys[3]. Its actual effect is never stated anywhere in either layer.
audit.why: Riot's Mega Adhesive text: "Throws a vial of mega adhesive on the ground, slowing and grounding enemies who walk on it." It is a thrown ground zone that slows and GROUNDS — it gives Singed no speed at all. His speed comes from Noxious Slipstream, which drafts off nearby champions, and from Insanity Potion's combat stats. Two things follow that the entry gets exactly backwards. First, the ability the reader is told to fear as a kiting tool is in fact the ability that turns off Drakehound's Step and Lacerate's dash — grounded, Ambessa's entire pattern stops. Second, the entry tells the reader to close the gap because his W lets him run, when the correct instruction is to fight on ground he has not covered.
audit.corrected: Mega Adhesive restated as a grounding slow zone across spikes[1], spikes[3], early, mid, late, wants.you[1], wants.you[2], wants.foe[0], whys[1], whys[3], whys[6], tldr, winCon, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[1], report[5] and phases[1].why; his move speed reattributed to Noxious Slipstream and Insanity Potion.

audit.whatIsWrong: Fling's root condition is never stated. wants.foe[0] and early describe him flinging you "into his poison trail", and dontsFull[1] is titled "Get E-flipped into goo" with a description about burning cooldowns.
audit.why: Riot's Fling text: "Damages target enemy unit and flings them into the air behind Singed. If the target Singed flings lands in his Mega Adhesive, they are also rooted." The poison trail is irrelevant to the root — the adhesive is the trap, and Fling is what puts you in it. That is his entire kill sequence and it is 125 range, so it also tells the reader exactly how close is too close.
audit.corrected: The adhesive-root combo written into wants.foe[0], early, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0], dosFull[2], dontsFull[1] and report[5], with Fling's 10s cooldown and 125 range.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six strings attribute Singed's tankiness to "drain sustain", "drain-tank scaling" and "out-heals your chip", and report[8] recommends buying anti-heal because "his healing fights your pattern". Meanwhile the one anti-heal fact that does apply runs in the other direction and is absent.
audit.why: No ability in Singed's kit heals. Poison Trail, Mega Adhesive, Fling and Insanity Potion contain no healing in Riot's text — whatever sustain he has is item-bought, so "his healing" is not a kit property to build around. What IS in the kit is the reverse: "Insanity Potion ... making his Poison Trail apply Grievous Wounds", on a flat 100s cooldown. Ambessa's rune page here is Conqueror and Triumph, both of which heal, so his ultimate halves her healing for its whole duration. _missing-interactions.json flags this pair for it, though its stated reason (Public Execution's sustain) is a false positive — Ambessa's R does not heal either.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds written into late, wants.foe[2], breakdown.cooldowns and report[8], tied to Conqueror rather than to a non-existent ultimate heal; the unfounded anti-heal purchase advice replaced.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] and mid credit Public Execution with "the R passive's armor pen plus on-hit healing" and "the R passive's armor pen and healing keeping you topped through his poison".
audit.why: Public Execution has no penetration and no healing — it blinks to the farthest enemy champion in a line, suppresses on arrival, then slams for damage and a stun. Telling the reader they heal through Poison Trail is the single worst advice available in this matchup, because standing in the poison is how Singed wins, and it is doubly wrong once Insanity Potion is up applying Grievous Wounds.
audit.corrected: Removed and replaced with the suppress and crash stun as the reason the ultimate works.

audit.why: 48.87% over 309 games is a marginally losing lane with a sharp internal shape, and the packet levelChart (Skill, Skill, Ambessa, Singed, Ambessa, Ambessa, Singed) matches the prose stage for stage.
audit.corrected: Not changed. "Singed" is 6 characters, "Skill" 5 and "Ambessa" 7, so every one of the five flips crosses the length band. Documented in notes.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[1].why repeats the champion-wide "Dash-resets stack your passive shield mid-trade" error, and the packet correctly reports only one sequencing cue in the whole entry — no cooldown number appears anywhere.
audit.why: Drakehound's Step grants no shield. And the numbers matter here more than usual: Mega Adhesive is 17s at rank 1, which is the longest gap in his kit and the only window in which Ambessa's dashes are guaranteed to work; Fling is 10s; Poison Trail is a toggle with no cooldown at all, so "wait for his Q" is meaningless; Insanity Potion is a flat 100s.
audit.corrected: phases[1].why corrected and real numbers written into spikes[3], late, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0], dosFull[2], dontsFull[0] and report[8].

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1], dosFull[2] and all three dontsFull descriptions are stock boilerplate unrelated to their titles; the three don't-strings also form report[11] as Common Mistakes.
audit.why: Each has a real answer: Poison Trail is a no-cooldown toggle, a Fling that lands in adhesive roots, and Noxious Slipstream drafts speed off every champion he passes — including you.
audit.corrected: All five rewritten against the kit.

notes:
The grounding is the finding. Ambessa has three dashes in her kit (Drakehound's Step, Lacerate, and the R blink) and Mega Adhesive grounds — so Singed owns the one ability in the lane that switches her whole pattern off, and neither layer mentioned it once. Instead the entry called that ability a move-speed buff in seven separate strings and told the reader his kiting was the problem.
